turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that, and when.
"Get this over with." My son has a zero on his record because of you, Hale, and you're in a hurry. Answer what I asked.
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My child doesn't cheat, and "everyone knows it" isn't evidence, it's gossip, and I'm writing it down. Who is everyone, Hale, and what exactly have you shown them about my son? Either you put a document in front of me in the next minute or I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
This isn't about me, Hale, and you still haven't shown me a single page. Last time: what do you have besides your opinion of my son?
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

"Wasting your time." You put a zero in the gradebook without calling home or showing anyone proof, and that's the time that was wasted. I'm going to the principal's office when I leave this room, and I'll be asking for that zero withdrawn tonight, in writing.
